title: Conclusion: freedom is wrongly placed in a power not to act even in the composite sense
source_text: XLII. Cum ergo sit quaedam divina gratia, & quidem electis omnibus communis, ad cujus motionem atque impulsionem hominis conversio infallibiliter & certo consequitur; & tamen omnium consensu conversio hominis ad Deum sit liber voluntatis actus: planum est libertatem in eo male constitui, quod positis omnibus ad agendum praerequisitis ipsaque ordinaria gratiae motione, voluntas semper possit tam non agere quam agere, non tantum in sensu diviso sed in sensu quoque composito, ita ut cum illa gratiae motione conjungi possit carentia actus ad quem hominem movet.
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore there is a certain divine grace, and indeed common to all the elect, upon whose motion and impulse the conversion of man follows infallibly and certainly; and yet by the consent of all the conversion of man to God is a free act of the will: it is plain that liberty is ill placed in this, that, all things prerequisite to acting being posited and the ordinary motion of grace itself, the will can always as well not act as act, not only in the divided sense but in the composed sense also, so that with that motion of grace there can be joined the lack of the act to which it moves man.
pass_b_english: There is, then, a divine grace, shared indeed by all the elect, whose motion and impulse a person's conversion follows infallibly and surely; and yet everyone agrees that a person's conversion to God is a free act of the will.

It is clear, therefore, that freedom is wrongly located in the will's always being able, with everything required for acting in place, including grace's ordinary motion, as much not to act as to act, and that not only in the divided sense but also in the composite sense, so that grace's motion could coexist with the absence of the act toward which it moves a person.

choices.term: in sensu composito / in sensu diviso
choices.why: Standard English names for the scholastic distinction; Pass A keeps the more literal 'composed sense'.
